Participant.description: Someone the network deals with. `type` says which kind, and decides which of the remaining fields apply: a node speaks Beckn and is addressed by its participantId; an upstream is an ordinary API our adapter calls. Permits additional properties because the registry re-validates the MERGED document on a PUT, and that document carries the osid, osUpdatedAt and osOwner the registry injected itself -- which a strict schema rejects as extraneous. Do not set this back to false without removing the update requests from the Postman collection.

baseUrl.description: The base something is appended to: a Beckn action for a node, a binding's path for an upstream. https for a node, since that is its wire identity; an upstream may be plaintext, because nothing in the registry is sent to it.

role.description: What this party does on the network, as a list. consumer asks. provider answers. network exposes publish and discover, answering discover from published catalogs. A network is ONE participant however many adapters it runs, so this says what the network serves rather than which process exists -- a split three-adapter deployment and a consolidated one carry the same value. Required on a node. Permitted on an upstream, where nothing reads it. Search it with `contains`, not `eq`: an exact match against a list finds nothing, while `contains` matches both a list and an older single-string value.

keys.description: Plural for rotation: an overlap where old and new are both valid. The sender names which it used by osid in the Authorization header. Required on a node, since a node's signatures are verified against them. Permitted on an upstream, which does not sign anything this stack verifies.

revision.description: The revision of the peer's descriptor this record was built from. Only ever increases: a descriptor offering a revision at or below the stored one is a replay and is refused, which is what stops a withdrawn or superseded declaration being presented as current. Applies to role network.

federationRole.description: What this entry is, in relation to us. source is a peer we consume from: our crawler asks it for its catalogs. requester is a peer that consumes from us: it calls us and we verify its signatures, but we do not crawl it. both is a peer in both directions, which is what mutual admission produces. This deployment's own entry carries none: it is identified from configuration. Absent on an entry written before this field existed, which is read as both. Applies to role network.

schemaPacks.description: The schema packs a peer network declared in its descriptor, stored verbatim. Recorded rather than interpreted: what a peer can speak is its statement, and rewriting it here would make our copy disagree with the document it was read from. The crawler derives the JSON-LD context URL it filters on from these, because a pack URL names the pack's attributes.yaml while a message is interpreted against the matching context.jsonld. Applies to role network.

projectionTtl.description: How long, in seconds, this peer permits us to keep what we crawled from it. Declared by the peer in its descriptor and recorded here verbatim: the network that owns the data decides how stale a copy of it may get, and a crawler that chose its own value would be deciding that for someone else. Always positive on a stored record -- a peer declaring 0 forbids caching entirely and is refused at admission rather than cached against its wishes. Applies to role network.

allOf.description: A node speaks Beckn: it needs a role and keys, and its id is its wire identity so it must be a hostname.

PublicKey.description: A public key, held as material: it is public, so there is nothing to protect. Identified by the osid the registry assigns on write -- which is what a sender names in the Authorization header, and so the only id a verifier can look up. alg carries the purpose: ed25519 signs, x25519 encrypts.

alg.description: The purpose, and the only thing that carries it now: ed25519 signs, x25519 encrypts. Both curves are 32-byte keys.

key.description: base64 of the 32 raw bytes: 44 chars, one trailing '='. Bare -- no encoding label in front of it. A truncated or wrong-curve key fails at write time.

validUntil.description: Absent means open-ended. Overlap with the next key's validFrom is the rotation window.

status.description: revoked withdraws the key early. Effective only once the reader refreshes.

ParticipantId.description: Stable id, and the only id. For a node this is its network identity -- what field 1 of the Authorization header names, and what a signature is verified against; for an upstream it is the Beckn offer.provider.id.

ParticipantType.description: node speaks Beckn. upstream is an API we call over ordinary HTTP and does not.
